title: Write draft-atwood-jmap-cid companion spec
description:
Write a JMAP Content Identifiers specification that adds cryptographic content hashes (SHA-256 and optionally multihash/CID) to JMAP blob and object metadata. The spec should be usable by all JMAP APIs, either as a standalone capability that any JMAP server can advertise, or as a basis for upstream PRs/issues against existing specs (RFC 8620 blob upload response, draft-ietf-jmap-filenode, draft-ietf-jmap-blobext).

The gap: JMAP blobIds are opaque server-assigned identifiers, not content-addressable. Clients browsing file trees, receiving attachments, or managing blobs have no way to verify integrity, detect duplicates, or use content-addressed storage patterns without downloading the full blob.

Scope:
- Session-level capability urn:ietf:params:jmap:cid
- Extension to blob upload response: sha256 (already in JMAP-CHAT upload), plus optionally a multihash or CID field
- Extension to FileNode objects: inline sha256 (or equivalent) on file nodes so clients can verify without downloading
- Extension to Blob/get (JMAP-BLOBEXT): hash properties returnable on demand
- IANA registration
- Design decision: SHA-256 only vs multihash (future-proof but complex)
- Design decision: standalone capability vs upstream patches to RFC 8620 / JMAP-FILENODE / JMAP-BLOBEXT

Intended outcome: either a publishable companion draft, or a concrete upstream issue/PR set filed against the relevant JMAP WG drafts.
close_reason: Draft written: draft-atwood-jmap-cid-00.md. Design decisions recorded in beads memory. SHA-256 only, standalone capability urn:ietf:params:jmap:cid.
